title: Do All Frames of Reference Have the Same Yardstick?
description: A research manuscript in general relativity. It asks whether all frames of reference share the same yardstick (ruler, clock and scale) and examines the premise that a black hole's event horizon is one boundary shared by every observer. Contents: the hidden yardstick assumption; the step-by-step derivation; why the horizon need not be shared without a common yardstick; different yardsticks inside the event horizon and how they allow escape; the boundary zone; why ruling out redshift inside the horizon is circular; simple proofs that observers A and B have different rulers, clocks and scales; formal ratio calculations between frames A, B, C and D; a worked numerical example; passing information through intermediate frames; time progression and the sign flip; conservation of momentum; granular against continuous universe; and a reviewer brief for theoretical physicists and AI evaluators. Part of the public section 'Physics: Particle Reconstruction and General Relativity'. Not peer-reviewed.
notes: Not peer-reviewed. First published on GitHub Pages on 21 November 2026.
